records.deidentified_narrative: on april 3, 2025, at approximately 1620hrs i, officer alford#2325, [school facility] [school facility] resource officer, was notified of an injured student. barnett student, jackson downing w/m dob [date], was injured after (not crossing where there was a crosswalk available) he ran between two park vehicles in the teachers parking lot ([school facility]) and ran into the passenger side of a moving vehicle (unit 1) traveling east through the parking lot at approximately 1612hrs. fellow classmate and friend, mia cedillo w/f dob [date], reported the incident. mia advised jackson ran into the side of a white vehicle, (later identified as a white 2018 audi a4 lp# [identifier]). jackson fell to the ground after coming into contact with the vehicle but immediately got up. the vehicle stopped and jackson waved at the driver to let them know that he was okay and then continued running northbound through the parking lot. the driver of the vehicle (later identified as raymond nguyen a/m dob **/**/**) waited for a few seconds and then continued eastbound through the parking lot. the vehicle turned northbound and circled back around looking for jackson unsuccessfully, because jackson had left the campus north of the parking lot. unit 1 left the location without further [school facility]'s video surveillance cameras (ipro 28 sensor 1 & 2 @ 1612hrs). a representative of jacksons family, [person] jr. w/m dob [date], was present on campus and was informed of what happened. [person] jackson to the schools main office where he received medical treatment from the schools nurse. ems arrived on scene (m23) and was allowed further treatment to jacksons injuries. initial diagnosis was a large contusion on jacksons right ankle (noticeable swelling) and abrasions on his left arm and knuckles. jackson was transported to cooks children (fort worth) where he received further medical attention. a business card with the report number was issued to [person]. the following day: based on vehicle registration ownership, i was able to cross reference the address of the vehicle to the schools address database. two students showed to attend barnett from the address, vivienne tran w/f dob [date] and vanessa tran w/f dob [date]. vanessa was summoned to my office. vanessa was sobbing and i asked her why was crying. she responded apologizing for what happened yesterday. i asked vanessa who was driving the vehicle, and she stated her cousin, raymond nguyen, a student at bowie high. vanessa stated jackson ran into the side of their vehicle. raymond attempted to stop but jackson eventually collided with the vehicle. jackson got up and ran away from the vehicle. vanessa left my office and returned to [school facility], officer regan davis#2842 and informed her of the incident. i requested that she interview raymond to get [roadway] and see if his vehicle sustained damage to where jackson collided with the vehicle. officer regan met with raymond who confirmed [roadway], please refer to her supplement to this report. all interviews were recorded on my bwc which were tagged, [school facility] video is available through aisd security. no further.

records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was traveling north on business interstate 35 in encinal tx. the pedestrian was walking east on sh 44 and business interstate 35 which is an intersection. unit 1 came into a stop at the intersection of business interstate 35 and sh 44. the pedestrian was walking east and crossing the railroad, meanwhile there was no crosswalk nor pedestrian signal. while it was still dark the pedestrian was walking in an area where light was hardly being illuminated. the pedestrian was also wearing dark clothing which made it difficult for the driver in unit 1 to notice the pedestrian. the pedestrian was also not wearing any reflectors in its clothing which is recommended especially when it is dark outside. unit 1 then proceeded after coming to a stop and made a left turn on sh 44 striking the pedestrian. both unit 1 and the pedestrian stayed at their destination where the incident occurred and waited for first responders to arrive.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling southbound through the walmart parking lot located at 521 s. central expy. anna, tx, approaching a three-way intersection within the lot. the intersection is controlled by protected stop signs in all directions and features clearly marked pedestrian crosswalks. as unit 1 entered the intersection, the driver did not come to a complete stop at the posted southbound stop sign and initiated a left turn to proceed eastbound through the lot. during the turn, the driver of unit 1 failed to observe a pedestrian who was actively crossing within the marked crosswalk. as a result, the front right quarter panel of unit 1 struck the pedestrian, causing the pedestrian to spin and fall to the ground. the pedestrian complained of leg pain at the scene but later declined transportation by ems to a medical facility. the driver of unit 1 stated he did not see the pedestrian in the crosswalk when executing the turn. no signs of intoxication or impairment were observed during contact with the driver. no damage was sustained to unit 1 from the impact. after the on-scene investigation was completed, both parties were released from the scene.

records.deidentified_narrative: i, officer r. agpalza with the whitney police department responded to [roadway], whitney tx for a auto pedestrian incident. i arrived on scene at 2103 hours, and made contact with a witness identified as robin prause # ([phone]). prause advised that the male subject identified as justin wright ([date]) was walking from the gas station and she observed a motorcycle later identified as unit#1 a black 2019 harley davidson txlp(300a9z) occupied by shawn rodriguez ([date]) going east bound towards hillsboro. prause further advised she saw a [roadway]. after gathering information i made contact with rodriguez while ems and fire made scene. rodriguez advised he was heading towards hillsboro and looked down at his fuel tank and that was all he could remember up to the crash. after speaking with rodriguez he was later transported to hillcrest, waco by careflite and i made contact with wright. prior to leaving by ambulance, a state trooper on scene had been advised by rodriguez he wanted big daddys wrecker to tow his vehicle. wright advised he was walking across from the gas station and that was when he was struck, wright was later transported to harris in fort worth, tx. after gathering this information i spoke with another male subject identified as robert lee ([phone]). lee advised he allowed rodriguez in front of him while he was driving east bound on jefferson just past the split in front of the tiger mart and further advised he observed the motorcycle wobble and wright in the air during the accident upon being struck and that he had called. after all information was gathered big daddys was dispatched and later took possession of the motorcycle and all units cleared and lanes opened

hrs, she was going from 3rd to 4th period from main campus to magnet center. pedestrian-gomez stated as she was walking across the middle crosswalk in the student parking lot an old black jeep (unit #1) was slowly moving forward through the crowd of students, [roadway] past the crosswalk. pedestrian-gomez stated the license plates on the front of the jeep (unit #1) were bent facing outward. pedestrian-gomez stated as she walked in front of the jeeps bumper the front license plates caught her pants and cut her right thigh as she was walking across, tearing her pants and causing a laceration approx. 5-inch in width. pedestrian-gomez stated the female student looked at her and then drove off. pedestrian-gomez stated girl was skinny, with medium short brown hair, wearing a white t shirt, and driving a dark colored old jeep (unit #1). the responding officer asked pedestrian-gomez if she knew the student who was driving or her name? pedestrian-gomez stated she did not know the girl or her name. i asked pedestrian-gomez if there were any credible witnesses that had seen the incident. pedestrian-gomez stated just a friend that she was walking with. i asked pedestrian-gomez how she felt when the license plates from the jeep (unit #1) struck her thigh? pedestrian-gomez stated at first, she didnt feel much but then later her thigh began to hurt. pedestrian-gomezs father aaron arturo gomez advised that on april 10, 2025, [school facility], he and his daughter located the jeep parked in the student parking lot and took pictures of the jeep. aaron arturo gomez provided magnet center (franklin hs ch1, april 10, 2025, at 02:35:54 pm to 02:36:26 pm) which revealed a black in color suv (unit #1) traveling north in the student parking lot and stops at the crosswalk for students crossing. unit #1 continues to travel slowly through the crowd of students in an attempt to cross the crosswalk. a large number of students can be seen crossing the crosswalk in the front and back of the suv (unit #1). simultaneously, unit #1 can be seen moving forward slowly through the crosswalk as students are walking all around the vehicle. pedestrian-gomez can be seen walking in front of unit #1 in attempt to cross. unit #1 can be seen slowly traveling, and pedestrian-gomez can be seen moving her right shoulder, as she walks closely by unit #1s front left bumper, as she continued to walk across the front bumper of unit #1. unit #1 can be seen passing by slowly and eventually leaves traveling north of the parking lot. pedestrian-gomez can be seen walking normally toward the franklin magnet campus with her friend. the video footage does not show the contact made with unit #1s license plates to pedestrian-torres right thigh and\or unable to view license plates due to the jeep on campus and that he was not able to positively identify the driver. the responding officer requested a registration check on tx-plates nfg-4708 in which came back to (owner) michelle flores, 6285 escondido el paso tx, 79912. the responding officer conducted a follow up at 6285 escondido in reference to this case. i officer j. deanda met with the resident renter richard rubalcava who advised that michelle flores does not reside at the residence and that nobody owns a jeep at his residence. the investigation revealed, the franklin surveillance video footage revealed unit #1 can be seen slowly traveling north bound crossing the crosswalk, and pedestrian-gomez can be seen moving her right shoulder, as she walks closely by unit #1s front left bumper, as she continued to walk across the front bumper of unit #1 without caution. after unit #1 passes by, pedestrian-gomez was seen walking toward the magnet campus normally and did not notify the driver of unit #1 of any type of incident. the video footage does not show the contact made with unit #1s license plates to pedestrian-gomez right thigh and\or unable to view license plates due to the distance and low quality of the records.public_safe_text: police responded to the above listed address in reference to a major accident involving a pedestrian. i arrived on scene and made contact with the pedestrian, who reported having pain on the right side of her body near her leg and shoulder. the pedestrian did not appear to have any life threatening injuries and was able to sit up on her own. the pedestrian informed me that she was walking from her motor vehicle through the parking lot towards the shops at la cantera when she was impacted on her right side by u1's motor vehicle. the pedestrian fell to the ground and did not report losing consciousness or hitting her head on the ground. i made contact with the driver of u1, who reported he was driving between 10 and 20mph through the parking lot and observed a group of pedestrians crossing in front of his vehicle. as the pedestrians passed the right side of u1's vehicle, he proceeded to move forward, where he impacted the listed pedestrian due to not paying attention to what was happening in front of him. the driver of u1 stopped and assisted the injured pedestrian until law enforcement arrived to proceed with the investigation. i inspected u1's motor vehicle for damage and did not observe any damage to the vehicle from the collision. i ran the vehicle license plate through tcic/ncic, which returned valid for registration and insurance. i ran u1's drivers license through tcic/ncic, which returned valid. i ran the pedestrians driver's license through tcic/ncic, which returned valid. both parties were provided with a case card and the pedestrian chose to seek medical treatment on her own and declined transport offered by medic 51 out of fear that the cost was too great.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was facing [roadway]. [roadway]. intersection. ped 1 was pushing child ped 2 in a stroller, preparing to travel south across the western crosswalk at the intersection. ped 1 could not be properly interviewed due to the pain she was expressing. d/u1 stated that she observed a green light and performed a right turn, believing the roadway was clear. d/u1 stated that she did not observe ped 1 nor ped 2 in the intersection. d/u1 advised that she observed the red stop hand illuminated on the walk sign when she performed the turn. upon my arrival u/1 was stopped very close to the area of impact, suggesting it was only traveling at relatively low speed. no tire marks were observed on the roadway. the stroller containing ped 2 did not appear to have significant damage and was still capable of both standing unassisted and rolling on its wheels. ped 1 was unwilling or unable to stand during police contact and was loaded onto a stretcher by safd. ped 2 was not in a significant state of distress, but a visible welt was seen on the left side of her forehead with minor bleeding. at least one unknown individual that called 911 indicated that ped 2 fell out of the stroller due to the impact. i observed several traffic light cycles during my investigation, and on each cycle it appears pedestrians making the crossing that ped 1 and ped 2 attempted are granted the right of way when unit 1 observed her green light. the walk cycle appears to move fairly quickly, cycling to the red stop hand and associated flashing countdown.
